question: Which desktop host presents the Essays UI while preserving the daemon as the only accepted-state semantic authority?
selected_option: Tauri v2 as a thin Rust-owned desktop shell over the daemon protocol, using packaged local UI assets, restrictive content policy, explicit window and WebView capabilities, and no accepted-state semantics in the shell.
rationale: The user explicitly selected OPT-DESKTOP-TAURI after the gate presented Tauri, a custom Wry shell, and Electron. Tauri preserves a Rust-owned native boundary and OS WebView footprint while avoiding the bespoke desktop lifecycle and security surface of a direct Wry shell.

required_semantics: the Tauri shell is a replaceable client and never implements accepted-state lifecycle, policy, revision, idempotency, capability, or effect rules
the shell communicates with the supervised daemon through the selected versioned local framed-JSON protocol
production windows load packaged local application assets; remote code execution in the privileged application WebView is prohibited
content security policy, navigation, new-window creation, external URL opening, custom protocols, downloads, and WebView permissions are deny-by-default and explicitly allowlisted
Tauri window and WebView capabilities expose only the narrow commands required by the focused writing client
the frontend has no ambient filesystem, process, shell, secret, credential, database, browser-driver, or network authority
all frontend messages are schema-validated and bound to the originating window or WebView before translation to canonical daemon requests
the supervised browser driver remains outside the Tauri application WebView and crosses its own explicit effect gate
OS-WebView differences are covered by platform-specific conformance evidence rather than assumed parity
non_implications: Tauri capabilities are a desktop containment layer and do not grant Essays semantic authority
selecting Tauri does not select the frontend framework, exact crates, plugin set, updater, signing, packaging, installer, or release channel
selecting Tauri does not make its WebView the supervised browser automation target
selecting Tauri does not authorize implementation, installation, network access, browser effects, publication, release, or deployment
the desktop selection does not prove startup speed, memory use, cross-platform parity, accessibility, security, or conformance

remaining_blockers: Essays security-owner review of the remote authentication binding
remote capability authorization and grant semantics
Product Capability decision and dependent contracts
authored ontology closure and DomainSpec generation
deferred_decisions: Frontend framework, exact Tauri and plugin versions, capability files, CSP bytes, custom protocol, daemon discovery UX, updater, signing, installers, and OS-WebView minimum versions are later implementation, security, platform, and release bindings.
